subject: userGWAS: warning "some estimated ov variances are negative", NA Qsnp

messages.author: b441d4df3af5ed92
messages.subject: userGWAS: warning "some estimated ov variances are negative", NA Qsnp
parts:
Hello everyone,

After getting a model with good fit for a second-order model, I ran userGWAS on the model. I encounter 2 issues that I really appreciate your insights.

All the SNPs have "some estimated ov variances are negative" warning, resulting from GWAS of the latent factors. Furthermore, for the second-order latent factor, every Qsnp is NA, and hence without Qsnp p-value.

This is my model:
"
F1 =~ T1 + T2 + T3 + T4 + T5
F2 =~ F1 + T6 + T7 + T8 + T9
F1 ~ SNP
F2 ~ SNP
"
The model fit statistics are chisq(df=27) = 454.8504, AIC = 490, CFI = 0.977, SRMR = 0.057.
None of the standardized factor loadings exceeds 1, and none of the standardized SE is negative. Hence, I didn't apply any constraints.
Upon inspection of the estimated variance for every trait for all SNPs, all of the estimated variance, for example T1~~T1, is positive.

Thank you in advance for the help!

Best regards,
Thanh Le

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: userGWAS: warning "some estimated ov variances are negative", NA Qsnp
parts:
Hi Thanh Le, 

Thanks for raising this! The new way of calculating factor-specific Qsnp uses as part of its calculation the difference (misfit) between the model implied SNP-trait covariances for the traits that load on that factor and the observed SNP-trait covariances. For a higher-order factor, those SNP-trait covariances are not observed for the lower-order factor used to define it, so the code is not currently written to be able to calculate Qsnp for higher-order factors. This is something that I've now documented on the wiki for this argument as below: 
"Note that this will not produce Q_SNP statistics for higher-order factors (i.e., latent factors defined by lower-order latent factors). For higher-order factors the Q_SNP statistic can be calculated by using the model chi-square difference test across the model where the SNP predicts the higher-order factor compared to a model where the SNP predicts the indicators of the higher-order factor." 

As noted there, you can still calculate Q_SNP for your F2 factor, but this will require running a second model where the SNP predicts the indicators of F2. 

Best, 
 Andrew
